newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's AMP says not interest in buying a bank.
newsitem.headline: Australia's AMP says not interest in buying a bank.

text.p: Australia's largest life office, the Australian Mutual Provident Society (AMP), managing director George Trumbull said on Monday the life office was not interested in acquiring an Australian bank.

The Australian-government commissioned Wallis report into the financial system, released last week, recommended an end to a ban on mergers between Australia's four major banks and the two biggest life offices.

Asked at a news conference if AMP was targetting the acquisition of a major Australian bank, Trumbull said: "None and never. We think the price of banks is pretty high -- We don't see it making much sense."
Trumbull said AMP already rented a banking licence and expected AMP would ultimately buy a banking licence of its own.
